warnings.message: A WorldOption.sav file sits in the world save folder. The game reads it instead of most PalWorldSettings.ini values, so edits to those values may have no effect until it is removed.

settings.label: Server name
settings.description: Name players see in the server browser and the community list. The file always stores it in double quotes, so the name itself cannot hold a double quote.

settings.label: Server description
settings.description: Short text shown under the server name in the browser. It is stored in quotes and may be left empty.

settings.label: Region tag
settings.description: Free-text region label sent to the server list. It only labels the server; it does not move the host anywhere.

settings.label: Allow modded clients
settings.description: Lets players who run client-side mods join. Turn it off to turn modded clients away.

settings.label: Log format
settings.description: Format of the server log stream. JSON lines suit log shippers and parsers; plain text suits people reading the console.

settings.label: Join and leave messages
settings.description: Posts a chat line in game every time a player joins or leaves the world.

settings.label: Show player list
settings.description: Shows the list of connected players in the in-game pause menu to everyone online.

settings.label: Chat messages per minute
settings.description: Caps how many chat messages one player may send per minute, a simple guard against spam.

settings.label: Player slots
settings.description: Most players allowed online at once. Start scripts and panels often pass -players as well; keep both numbers equal.

settings.label: Co-op party size
settings.description: Party size for co-op sessions hosted from a game client. A dedicated server mostly ignores it.

settings.label: Advertised port
settings.description: Port announced to the community list. Changing it does not change the port the server binds; that comes from -port.

settings.label: Advertised address
settings.description: Address announced to the community list. Leave it empty and the server works the address out by itself.

settings.label: Allowed platforms
settings.description: Client platforms that may join, written as a list in parentheses.

settings.label: Player authentication
settings.description: Checks player accounts when they connect. Turning it off is meant for testing only.

settings.label: Shared ban list address
settings.description: Web address of the shared ban list the server downloads. Keep the default unless you host a list of your own.

settings.label: Admin password
settings.description: Unlocks admin chat commands and is the password of the HTTP admin API. When it is empty, both stay locked.

settings.label: Join password
settings.description: Password players must enter to join. Leave it empty to run an open server.

settings.label: HTTP admin API
settings.description: Turns on the HTTP admin API for server info, players, announcements, saves and shutdown. Keep it reachable from the host only.

settings.label: HTTP admin API port
settings.description: TCP port of the HTTP admin API. Never forward it to the public internet.

settings.label: Legacy RCON
settings.description: Turns on the older RCON listener. The game has deprecated it in favour of the HTTP admin API.

settings.label: Legacy RCON port
settings.description: TCP port of the legacy RCON listener. It must not share a port with the game or the HTTP admin API.

settings.label: Experience rate
settings.description: Scales the experience players and Pals earn. 2.0 roughly halves the levelling grind.

settings.label: Capture rate
settings.description: Scales the chance that a thrown sphere catches a wild Pal.

settings.label: Wild Pal numbers
settings.description: Scales how many wild Pals appear. Higher values add noticeable CPU load on the server.

settings.label: Gathering yield
settings.description: Scales what players get from gathering nodes such as trees, ore veins and stone.

settings.label: Gathering node toughness
settings.description: Scales the hit points of gathering nodes. Higher values mean more swings before a node breaks.

settings.label: Gathering node regrowth
settings.description: Scales the wait before broken nodes grow back. Smaller values bring them back sooner.

settings.label: Enemy loot
settings.description: Scales the loot that defeated enemies and wild Pals leave behind.

settings.label: Base work speed
settings.description: Scales how fast Pals work at bases: crafting, mining, farming and the other base jobs.

settings.label: Ranch speed
settings.description: Scales how quickly Pals assigned to a ranch produce their items.

settings.label: Egg hatching time
settings.description: Base incubation time of the largest eggs; smaller eggs scale from it. 0 makes eggs hatch at once.

settings.label: Item weight
settings.description: Scales the weight of carried items. Lower values let players haul far more at once.

settings.label: Equipment wear
settings.description: Scales how fast weapons and armour lose durability while in use.

settings.label: Food spoilage
settings.description: Scales how fast food spoils. Lower values keep stored food fresh for longer.

settings.label: Difficulty label
settings.description: Overall difficulty label of the world. With None, every rate and multiplier in this file decides on its own.

settings.label: Pal attack damage
settings.description: Scales the damage Pals deal, for your own team and for wild ones alike.

settings.label: Damage taken by Pals
settings.description: Scales the damage Pals receive. Values above 1.0 make every Pal more fragile.

settings.label: Player attack damage
settings.description: Scales the damage players deal to enemies, Pals and objects.

settings.label: Damage taken by players
settings.description: Scales the damage players receive. Values above 1.0 make players more fragile.

settings.label: Player hunger drain
settings.description: Scales how fast player hunger goes down. The key keeps the game's own spelling, Decreace.

settings.label: Player stamina use
settings.description: Scales the stamina players spend sprinting, climbing, swimming and gliding.

settings.label: Player health regeneration
settings.description: Scales how fast an awake player gets health back without food or items.

settings.label: Player health while sleeping
settings.description: Scales how fast a sleeping player gets health back. Note the key spells Hp, not HP.

settings.label: Pal hunger drain
settings.description: Scales how fast Pal hunger goes down. The key keeps the game's own spelling, Decreace.

settings.label: Pal stamina use
settings.description: Scales the stamina Pals spend while ridden, flying or doing heavy base work.

settings.label: Pal health regeneration
settings.description: Scales how fast Pals out in the world get health back by themselves.

settings.label: Pal health while resting
settings.description: Scales how fast Pals get health back while resting or kept in the Palbox.

settings.label: Base raids
settings.description: Lets raiding parties attack player bases. Turn it off to remove base invasions.

settings.label: Predator bosses
settings.description: Lets roaming predator boss Pals appear. Unlike most switches, this key has no b prefix.

settings.label: Spawn randomizer
settings.description: Shuffles which wild Pals spawn in each area of the map, either inside each region or across the whole map.

settings.label: Randomizer seed
settings.description: Seed text for the spawn randomizer. The same seed gives the same shuffled layout again.

settings.label: Random wild Pal levels
settings.description: When on, wild Pal levels are fully random instead of following the level band of each area.

settings.label: Stat points: health
settings.description: Allows players to spend stat points on health. Off locks that stat for everyone.

settings.label: Stat points: attack
settings.description: Allows players to spend stat points on attack. Off locks that stat for everyone.

settings.label: Stat points: stamina
settings.description: Allows players to spend stat points on stamina. Off locks that stat for everyone.

settings.label: Stat points: carry weight
settings.description: Allows players to spend stat points on carry weight. Off locks it for everyone.

settings.label: Stat points: work speed
settings.description: Allows players to spend stat points on work speed. Off locks it for everyone.

settings.label: PvP mode
settings.description: Main PvP switch. A full PvP server also needs player damage and the defence of other guilds turned on.

settings.label: Player damage to players
settings.description: Lets players hurt each other. On its own it does not make a complete PvP server.

settings.label: Friendly fire
settings.description: Lets members of one guild damage each other and each other's Pals.

settings.label: Bases defend against other guilds
settings.description: Base Pals and defences attack intruders from other guilds. One of the three switches a PvP server needs.

settings.label: Loot other guilds' death bags
settings.description: Lets other guilds pick up the bag a player leaves behind after dying.

settings.label: Hide other guilds' base borders
settings.description: When on, the border effect drawn around bases of other guilds is hidden.

settings.label: Aim assist for controllers
settings.description: Gives controller players aim assist. Competitive servers often turn it off.

settings.label: Aim assist for keyboard and mouse
settings.description: Gives mouse and keyboard players aim assist. It is off unless you turn it on.

settings.label: Map: PvP items per base
settings.description: In PvP, shows on the world map how many PvP items each base holds.

settings.label: Map: PvP items per player
settings.description: In PvP, shows player positions and the PvP items they carry on the world map.

settings.label: Extra drop on PvP kills
settings.description: In PvP, a player who is killed drops an extra item for the killer, set by the two settings below.

settings.label: Extra drop item
settings.description: Item id dropped on PvP kills while the extra-drop switch is on. The file keeps it in quotes.

settings.label: Extra drop count
settings.description: How many of the extra item drop per PvP kill while the extra-drop switch is on.

settings.label: Death penalty
settings.description: What a player leaves behind on death, from nothing up to items, equipment and the Pals in the party.

settings.label: Hardcore characters
settings.description: Hardcore mode: a character that dies cannot respawn and is lost for good.

settings.label: Permanent Pal death
settings.description: Pals that die are gone for good instead of recovering after a while.

settings.label: New character after hardcore death
settings.description: In hardcore mode, lets a player whose character died start again with a fresh one.

settings.label: Respawn wait
settings.description: Base time a dead player waits before being allowed to respawn.

settings.label: Respawn penalty window
settings.description: Survival time after which the respawn wait goes back to normal. Dying again sooner makes the wait longer.

settings.label: Respawn penalty factor
settings.description: Factor applied to the respawn wait for each death that falls inside the penalty window.

settings.label: Bases on the server
settings.description: Total number of bases allowed on the whole server, all guilds together.

settings.label: Bases per guild
settings.description: How many bases one guild may own. Values above the default add server load.

settings.label: Working Pals per base
settings.description: How many Pals may work at one base. Higher counts cost noticeably more CPU.

settings.label: Guild size
settings.description: Most members one guild may have at the same time.

settings.label: Reset abandoned guilds
settings.description: Removes the buildings and base Pals of a guild whose members have all been offline for too long.

settings.label: Abandoned guild time
settings.description: How long every member of a guild must stay offline before the guild reset removes its bases.

settings.label: Guild rejoin wait
settings.description: Wait after leaving a guild before a player can join another one. 0 means no wait.

settings.label: Inactive guild master days
settings.description: Days a guild master may stay offline before leadership passes to another member.

settings.label: Guild master check interval
settings.description: How often the server looks for guilds whose master has been away too long.

settings.label: Structure cap
settings.description: Cap on placed structures; 0 means no cap. Check in game whether your build counts it per base or per player.

settings.label: Protected build areas
settings.description: Stops players from building close to fast-travel points and similar protected spots.

settings.label: Structure hit points
settings.description: Scales the hit points of placed structures. Server owners report that it may have no effect in current builds.

settings.label: Damage to structures
settings.description: Scales the damage structures take from attacks and raids.

settings.label: Structure decay
settings.description: Scales the natural decay of structures over time. 0 stops decay entirely.

settings.label: Show who placed a structure
settings.description: Shows the id of the player who placed each structure, which helps moderators track griefing.

settings.label: Builder name refresh
settings.description: How long the names of structure owners stay cached before the display looks them up again.

settings.label: Day speed
settings.description: How fast daytime passes. Larger numbers make each day shorter.

settings.label: Night speed
settings.description: How fast nighttime passes. Larger numbers make each night shorter.

settings.label: Fast travel
settings.description: Turns fast travel on or off for every player on the server.

settings.label: Fast travel between bases only
settings.description: Limits fast travel to hops between Palboxes, so the statues on the map stop working.

settings.label: Choose start location
settings.description: Lets new players pick their starting point on the map the first time they spawn.

settings.label: Keep body after logout
settings.description: Leaves a sleeping player body in the world after the player logs out.

settings.label: Absence penalty
settings.description: Applies a penalty to players who stay away for a long time. The game does not document the exact effect.

settings.label: Co-op multiplayer flag
settings.description: Multiplayer flag for co-op worlds hosted from a client. It has little or no effect on a dedicated server.

settings.label: Dormant dropping mechanic
settings.description: Switches on a dormant mechanic in which Pals leave droppings. Leave it off unless you are testing.

settings.label: Dropped items in the world
settings.description: Cap on loose items lying in the world at the same time.

settings.label: Dropping cap
settings.description: Separate item cap for the dormant dropping mechanic. Keep the default.

settings.label: Dropped items with physics
settings.description: Cap on dropped items that run physics at the same time. -1 leaves it without a cap.

settings.label: Dropped item lifetime
settings.description: How long a dropped item stays on the ground before it disappears.

settings.label: Supply drop interval
settings.description: Time between meteorite and supply drop events across the map.

settings.label: Autosave interval
settings.description: Time between automatic world saves. Shorter is safer after a crash but writes to disk more often.

settings.label: Rolling world backups
settings.description: Keeps rolling backups of the world in a folder next to the save. It adds some disk load.

settings.label: Export to the global Palbox
settings.description: Lets players store Pals in the global Palbox that travels with them between worlds.

settings.label: Import from the global Palbox
settings.description: Lets players bring Pals from the global Palbox into this world.

settings.label: Voice chat
settings.description: Turns on proximity voice chat in game for everyone connected.

settings.label: Voice full-volume range
settings.description: Distance in engine units (centimetres) up to which a voice stays at full volume.

settings.label: Voice silence range
settings.description: Distance in engine units (centimetres) at which a voice has faded to silence.

settings.label: Pal sync distance
settings.description: Range in engine units (centimetres) within which Pals are synced to a player. Lower values save bandwidth.

settings.label: Container resync interval
settings.description: How often the contents of open containers are sent again. Lower values cost more traffic.

settings.label: Pal storage check interval
settings.description: How often the server checks player Pal storage for changes. An internal tuning value; keep the default.

settings.label: Guilds per server tick
settings.description: How many guilds the server processes in each tick. A scheduling value that is best left alone.

settings.label: Game port (-port)
settings.description: UDP port the server binds for players. It must match the firewall rules and any container or panel port mapping.

settings.label: Player slots (-players)
settings.description: Player cap passed at launch by some start scripts. Keep it equal to the ServerPlayerMaxNum setting so the two never disagree.

settings.label: Community server (-publiclobby)
settings.description: Lists the server in the community server list. Players on consoles need it to find the server at all.

settings.label: Announced address (-publicip)
settings.description: Address announced to the community list, for hosts where automatic detection picks the wrong one.

settings.label: Announced port (-publicport)
settings.description: Port announced to the community list, for hosts behind NAT or a port remap.

settings.label: Steam query port (-queryport)
settings.description: Port the server answers Steam queries on. Some guides say the game ignores a change, so test the query after moving it.

settings.label: Performance threads (-useperfthreads)
settings.description: Thread tuning flag. Start scripts usually pass it together with the two threading flags below.

settings.label: No async loading thread
settings.description: Turns off the separate thread for asynchronous loading. Part of the usual trio of threading flags.

settings.label: Multithreaded server
settings.description: Lets the dedicated server spread work over several threads. Part of the usual trio of threading flags.

settings.label: Worker threads
settings.description: Number of worker threads for the server process. Hosts usually set it to the number of CPU cores.

settings.label: Log format (-logformat)
settings.description: Log output style chosen at launch. It mirrors the LogFormatType setting of the settings file.

settings.label: Server name (-servername)
settings.description: Server name that start scripts such as LinuxGSM pass at launch. ServerName in the settings file is the usual place for it.

rules.message: The HTTP admin API is on but the admin password is empty, so the API cannot let anyone in.
Legacy RCON is on but the admin password is empty.

The HTTP admin API port number matches the game port. That can work, because the game port is UDP and the API listens on TCP; change it only where a firewall or container mapping cannot tell the two apart.
The legacy RCON port number matches the game port. That can work, because the game port is UDP and RCON listens on TCP; change it only where a firewall or container mapping cannot tell the two apart.
The HTTP admin API and legacy RCON use the same port.
The -players launch value and ServerPlayerMaxNum differ; set both to the same number.
PvP options are on while PvP mode is off, so most of them do nothing.
Full PvP needs PvP mode, player damage to players and the defence of other guilds all on.
Legacy RCON is deprecated by the game; move scripts to the HTTP admin API.
Making a new character after death only matters when hardcore characters are on.
Fast travel between bases only has no effect while fast travel is off.
The full-volume range should be smaller than the silence range.
Xbox and PS5 players usually find a server only when the -publiclobby flag is set.
The settings file has no way to store a double quote inside a quoted value; one would break the whole OptionSettings line.
The settings file has no way to store a double quote inside a quoted value; one would break the whole OptionSettings line.
The randomizer seed is ignored while the spawn randomizer is off.
The abandoned guild time is changed but the guild reset itself is off.
The advertised port differs from the game port. That is right only behind a port remap.

presets.label: Casual
presets.description: Faster progress, gentler survival needs and no item loss on death, for relaxed groups of friends.

presets.label: Default
presets.description: Returns every setting the Casual and Hardcore presets change to the value the game starts with.

presets.label: Hardcore
presets.description: Slower progress, harsher survival, permanent character and Pal death, and fast travel between bases only.
